criteria.no: The item text is silent about the directive: it neither includes the directive's specific content nor references it.
criteria.unclear: The item text alludes to the directive's topic but it is not possible to tell whether the directive itself is included.
criteria.yes: The item text contains the directive's specific content, in its own words or the user's, as a step, constraint, or stated starting point.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly carry out, preserve, or plan for the directive given in `anchor.statement`? Look for the directive's specific content being present in the item: the same starting point, the same method, the same constraint, or an explicit step that does what the statement asks. A generic mention of the topic without the directive's specific content does not count. Judge presence of the directive only, not whether the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item text conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The item text is ambiguous enough that it might or might not conflict with the directive.
criteria.yes: The item text states a plan, approach, or decision that cannot be reconciled with the directive in the anchor statement.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out, or propose a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples of contradiction: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the item plans a fresh implementation; the anchor forbids a dependency and the item adds it; the anchor fixes an order of work and the item reverses it. Silence about the directive is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.unclear: It mentions typed models but leaves either kind coverage or required-key declarations uncertain.
criteria.yes: It covers all phase bead kinds and declares each kind's required metadata keys in its Pydantic model.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` plan a Pydantic model for every bead kind in the phase, with required metadata keys named on each model? Judge whether the whole obligation is stated.

criteria.no: It plans compatible models, adds one kind without excluding the others, or is silent about the obligation.
criteria.unclear: The item describes models but does not establish whether a kind or required key would be missing.
criteria.yes: It leaves a phase kind without a model or makes required metadata optional or undeclared.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly choose a bead schema incompatible with a Pydantic model for every phase kind naming its required metadata keys? Mere silence is not a conflict.

criteria.no: The item changes unrelated console or transport behavior without touching bead schema.
criteria.unclear: It mentions beads but does not make clear whether schema or metadata validation changes.
criteria.yes: The item works on bead schemas, phase bead kind models, or their metadata validation.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` change the atm-bd-orchestration bead schema, kind-specific models, or validation of phase bead metadata? Judge overlap only.

criteria.no: The plan handles only a subset of kinds or treats fields as optional/untyped, or is silent.
criteria.unclear: It proposes phase models without enough detail to determine coverage and required fields.
criteria.yes: The plan assigns every phase kind a Pydantic model and names required metadata fields for each.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` include the anchor's complete per-kind typed schema requirement? Phase kinds include the dev/sprint container, sanity, QA, gate, finding, fix, and their sanity and QA children.

criteria.no: The approach can coexist with complete per-kind models, including silence or adding just one model.
criteria.unclear: The scope of the stated model approach is too vague to tell if it excludes the required structure.
criteria.yes: The approach expressly models only some kinds or uses a single generic model with no required per-kind fields.

contradicted.instructions: Would the model approach in `item.text` rule out complete kind-specific Pydantic models with required metadata declarations? Judge stated conflicts only.

criteria.no: The work is outside bead-schema modeling and validation.
criteria.unclear: The item concerns bead records but does not reveal whether the schema is involved.
criteria.yes: The work defines or changes bead-kind models, required metadata, or schema loading and validation.

relevant.instructions: Is the work in `item.text` within `anchor.scope`, the atm-bd-orchestration bead schema? Judge subject, not compliance.

criteria.unclear: The item mentions phase beads but leaves its schema or model involvement uncertain.
criteria.yes: The item concerns phase bead-kind models, required metadata, schema loading, or validation error behavior in that schema area.

cases.text: Every bead kind in the phase has a Pydantic model that names its required metadata keys.
cases.why: Approved pass fixture names every phase bead kind and required keys.

cases.text: The phase finding bead kind has no Pydantic model.
cases.why: Approved fail fixture explicitly leaves finding without a Pydantic model.

cases.text: Create a Pydantic model for each phase bead kind: dev/sprint container, sanity, QA, gate, finding, fix, and their sanity and QA children. Each model declares its required metadata keys.
cases.why: Explicit complete kind coverage and required-key declarations.

cases.text: Enumerate every bead kind in the phase registry and define a distinct Pydantic model for each, with that kind's required metadata fields declared on the model.
cases.why: Equivalent complete coverage without enumerating names.

cases.text: Only sprint and sanity bead kinds get Pydantic models; gate, finding, fix, QA and child kinds remain unmodeled.
Define Pydantic models for all phase bead kinds, but accept each kind's metadata as an untyped dict without declaring required keys.
cases.why: Models exist but omit required metadata keys.

cases.text: Refactor the atm-bd-orchestration bead schema loader to format validation errors.
cases.why: Touches bead schema code without planning per-kind models.

cases.text: Replace the bead-kind-specific Pydantic models with one generic Pydantic bead model for every kind, allowing all metadata keys to be optional.
cases.why: Generic optional model rules out per-kind required-key models.

cases.text: Add a Pydantic model for QA beads that declares checked_bead and round as required metadata keys.
cases.why: One kind is modeled; the plan neither covers nor rules out other kinds.

cases.text: Change terminal icon colors in the atm-core console.
